description: Offline-first resilience network for blackouts and disasters - phone mesh, on-device Claude, Solana proof.

detail.readme:
# 8LACKOUT ### Keep a city coordinating when the lights go out. An offline-first resilience network for blackouts, disasters, and war zones. Phones form their own radio mesh, an on-device Claude runs the coordination, and every action is proven on Solana the moment any signal returns. [![mesh](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-LoRa%20%2B%20BLE%20mesh-111)](#) [![ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-on--device%20Claude-111)](#) [![chain](https://img.shields.io/badge/ledger-Solana%20(offline)-111)](#) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-111)](#)
--- ## What it is https://8lackout.com/ When the grid, the towers, or the internet go down, coordination dies first. 8LACKOUT assumes they're already off. It turns a pile of ordinary phones and a few cheap radios into a working command layer: people find each other, needs get matched to responders, aid is proven, and the record of what happened survives — all with no internet, no cell, no cloud. > Civilian infrastructure only. No targeting, no surveillance. It keeps people findable, aid accountable, and the truth timestamped when every normal system is down. --- ## The tool `8lackout` is a single binary that turns any device into a node. Same command on a phone, a laptop, or a solar beacon — it finds whatever radios are present and joins the mesh. ```bash # install curl -fsSL https://get.8lackout.net | sh # bring a node online (auto-detects LoRa / BLE / any uplink) 8lackout up --name "ward-7-clinic" # post a need — the on-device operator structures and localizes it 8lackout need "insulin, 2 people, Khoroolol 4, building 12" # see what's live on the mesh around you 8lackout board # claim and deliver, co-signing proof on handoff 8lackout claim 8lackout deliver --with ``` Most people never touch the CLI — they open the **app** (an offline PWA: map, needs board, QR handoff, scanner). The CLI is what runs the beacons and lets power users script the network. --- ## How it works - **Mesh, no towers.** Nodes talk over LoRa radio and Bluetooth, relaying for each other so a message hops across a neighborhood with zero infrastructure. Any real uplink anywhere (one satellite phone, one bar of signal) heals the whole mesh. - **The operator runs offline.** A quantized Claude model lives on the device. It triages needs, translates at checkpoints, and turns a panicked voice note into a structured, routable request — with no connection. When a link returns, the full Claude verifies and co-signs the record. - **Proof that can't be faked.** Every delivery is co-signed by both sides as a proof-of-aid record using Solana durable nonces — valid while fully offline. Donors and coordinators later see exactly what reached whom. - **A record nobody can erase.** Event hashes, evidence, and the blackout timeline commit to an immutable ledger, so the account of what happened outlives the blackout. | Layer | Normal assumption | 8LACKOUT | |---|---|---| | **Network** | Towers + ISP | LoRa + BLE mesh, phone-to-phone relay | | **AI** | Cloud API | On-device Claude, offline; full Claude co-signs on reconnect | | **Trust** | Bank / online RPC | Solana txns pre-signed with durable nonces, gossiped over mesh, settled on reconnect | | **Scale** | One row per event | State compression → millions of aid receipts for pennies | | **Power** | The grid | Solar beacons as always-on anchor relays | The whole trick: **nothing needs connectivity at the moment of action.** You sign, log, and coordinate locally; the network reconciles later, and the chain is the referee that makes the offline record trustworthy after the fact. --- ## Architecture ``` ┌──────────── OFFLINE (the blackout) ────────────┐ ┌─ ONLINE (signal returns) ─┐ │ │ │ │ voice / ┌─────────┐ LoRa/BLE mesh ┌─────────┐ durable-nonce ┌──────────┐ settle + verify ┌──────────┐ text ──▶│ app PWA │◀────gossip───────▶│ app PWA │──signed txns────▶│ beacon │──────batch───────▶│ Solana │ │ + agent │ │ + agent │ │ (solar) │ │ programs │ └────┬────┘ └────┬────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ │ on-device Claude │ relay for peers │ store-and-forward │ proof-of-aid ▼ triage / translate ▼ ▼ holds queue until uplink ▼ receipts + timeline ``` ``` 8lackout/ ├── cli/ # the `8lackout` binary — node, needs, claim, deliver, beacon ├── mesh/ # radio firmware + relay daemon (LoRa, BLE, WebRTC bridge) ├── agent/ # on-device Claude: triage, translation, voice→structured need ├── chain/ # Solana programs: proof-of-aid, durable-nonce queue, receipts, timeline ├── app/ # offline-first PWA (map, needs board, QR handoff, scanner) ├── beacon/ # solar anchor node (store-and-forward, uplink reconciler) └── docs/ # threat model, field guide, protocol spec ``` ### The three flows 1. **Need → match.** Someone posts a need; the on-device agent structures and localizes it; it's gossiped across the mesh; a nearby responder claims it. 2. **Deliver → prove.** On handoff, both phones co-sign a proof-of-aid record (durable nonce, fully offline). It rides the mesh toward a beacon. 3. **Reconnect → settle.** When a beacon gets any uplink, it batches the queue to Solana: receipts commit, the day's timeline is co-signed by the full Claude, and coordinators see verified aid. --- ## Run a beacon A beacon is any always-on node with power and an antenna — a Raspberry Pi with a LoRa hat and a solar panel is enough. It stores and forwards the mesh when phones go dark and reconciles everything to chain when it gets a link. ```bash 8lackout beacon --solar --uplink auto ``` --- ## Principles - Civilians first. No targeting, no surveillance, no offensive use. - Offline is the default; online is the exception. - The chain exists to make an offline record trustworthy — not to require connectivity. - Open source, auditable, forkable. MIT.
